A2.value: Definitions, decision rules, category logic, ID conventions and evidence standards applied across the combined workbook

B6.value: External-trends assessment for U.S. credit unions over a 3–5 year horizon. It combines AI-related and non-AI risks but does not assess VyStar controls, current exposure, residual risk, owners or actual matches to VyStar’s Risk Register.

B7.value: A new or materially changing external uncertainty that could alter the nature, scale, speed or connectivity of exposure and has a defensible mechanism, pathway, consequence and evidence base.

B8.value: Retain a separate row only when the candidate has an independent mechanism of emergence, exposure/pathway, consequence, evidence base and distinction from other risks. Otherwise merge, reclassify or remove it and record the decision in Challenge Log.

B9.value: Risk = uncertain exposure with adverse consequence. Emerging Threat = developing hostile or destabilizing external hazard. Risk Driver = a condition changing another risk and is not retained as a standalone row without its own pathway. Opportunity = independent value-creation pathway; linked opportunities are normally captured within the relevant risk row.

B10.value: Authoritative, preferably recent primary evidence; corroboration where practical; consistent findings; and observed facts, events or operative requirements with limited dependence on forecast assumptions.

B11.value: Credible evidence and a plausible mechanism, but credit-union-specific data, adoption pace, transferability or consequence magnitude remains incomplete or forecast-dependent.

B12.value: Plausible weak signal supported mainly by sparse, indirect or speculative evidence. Retain only where the pathway or preparation lead time justifies monitoring and uncertainty is explicit.

B13.value: One dominant type per risk, based on the evidence supporting its central mechanism. Observed Trend = repeated or measured directional pattern. Fact = documented discrete event, test result, current condition or operative requirement. Expert Assessment = reasoned interpretation without a directly established full pathway. Forecast = explicit forward estimate. Weak Signal / Speculative Hypothesis = plausible but unestablished pathway. A test result is a Fact about the test, not proof of financial losses. Selection rationale is in Assessment Evidence.

B14.value: Time from a risk event, trigger or control failure to material organizational impact. It is not likelihood, time until the trend appears, or duration of the resulting loss.

B15.value: Use when the fastest credible, evidence-supported pathway can produce material impact immediately or within one year after the trigger, including transaction-speed fraud, cyber intrusion, liquidity outflow or an authorized agent action.

B16.value: 13–18 months: supported first material impact occurs in this post-trigger interval. Do not classify the time to adoption, implementation before the trigger, or future regulation as risk velocity. Current row assignments are preserved; this update does not validate all historical assignments.

B17.value: Over 18 months: evidence supports a post-trigger delay beyond 18 months. A distant technology arrival, transition deadline or demographic horizon alone is insufficient. Unsupported finer timing remains Unknown in Velocity Rationale.

B18.value: Use when current evidence does not support a defensible assignment. Unknown is preferable to false precision. A long-horizon trend can still have fast velocity if impact accelerates after a trigger.

B19.value: Immediate = High/Medium evidence, 0–12 month velocity and current action relevance. Near-Term = preparation is warranted within the next planning cycle. Monitor = credible structural risk requiring periodic review. Watch / Validate = Low evidence or weak signal. No quantitative likelihood or impact scores are fabricated.

B20.value: Ordinal rank within the assigned Risk Category only. Combined ranks are ordered by Priority, then Velocity, Evidence Strength and directness of the external pathway. Rank 1 is the highest-priority risk in that category; it is not an enterprise risk score.

B21.value: Assign the category of the primary loss event or first material organizational consequence, not the technology, driver, control weakness or every downstream effect. Cross-category effects remain in Interdependencies, Existing Risk Mapping and Expected Impact.

B22.value: Primary pathway is violation, enforcement, litigation, legal uncertainty or inability to meet an operative obligation.

B23.value: Primary pathway is borrower repayment stress, collateral deterioration, underwriting error or portfolio loss.

B24.value: Primary pathway is earnings or economic-value sensitivity caused by repricing, duration, deposit-behavior or rate-model change.

B25.value: Primary pathway is inability or excessive cost to meet cash obligations at the required speed.

B26.value: Primary pathway is loss of trust or confidence that directly changes member or stakeholder behavior; downstream liquidity effects are linked separately.

B27.value: Primary pathway is business-model, competitive, workforce, channel or investment-position failure over the horizon.

B28.value: Primary pathway is failed processes, people, systems, cyber events, models, vendors, infrastructure or transaction execution.

B29.value: Use a measurable threshold only when supported by an external standard or an internally approved appetite. Otherwise label a Judgment-Based Trigger. Internal thresholds should be added during later VyStar mapping, not invented here.

B30.value: Priority order: NCUA and credit-union evidence; U.S. government and regulators; transferable banking evidence; academic and recognized industry research. Prefer the latest 12 months, retaining older sources when operative, foundational or not superseded.

B31.value: Each risk is challenged for slower adoption, stabilizing factors, mitigating controls, conflicting forecasts and evidence weakness. Counter-evidence can change confidence or priority without automatically removing the risk.

B32.value: Risk IDs use ER-1, ER-2… and Source IDs use S-1, S-2… with no leading zeros. IDs are stable text keys for LogicGate integration. Multi-value ID fields use semicolon-plus-space delimiters.

B33.value: AI-related identifies risks whose emerging mechanism materially depends on AI. Non-AI identifies risks retained independently of AI. The field is explicit so API consumers do not infer scope from the risk name.

B34.value: Original AI research: September 9, 2026; non-AI: September 16. Evidence Type, conditional timing, outlook and selected source status updated September 24, 2026. Horizon for the outlook: 2029–2031. Imported model maturity/link decisions retain their September 18 review basis.

B35.value: ≤24 hours; >24 hours–7 days; >7–30 days; >30–90 days; >90–180 days; >180–365 days; >365 days. A source may support a span across bands (e.g., ≤30 days). Explicitly label observed chronology, analogy or mechanism inference. If unsupported: Unknown — Insufficient evidence to refine the interval.

B36.value: Risk Velocity values and original qualitative priorities are preserved as requested. A faster supported conditional pathway is flagged Band review needed; absent timing evidence is Timing unvalidated in Assessment Evidence. Model Scores uses retained broad bands and must be read with these limitations.

B37.value: Analyst forecast of external pressure over 3–5 years from September 24, 2026. Increasing = evidence-supported drivers are expected to strengthen pressure; Constant = affirmative baseline of broadly persistent pressure; Decreasing = evidence-supported net easing; Unknown = conflicting or insufficient evidence. Unknown is not Constant. No forecast of VyStar exposure or residual risk.

B38.value: State the dominant drivers, geographic/sector transfer limits, opposing evidence and source IDs. Current observations anchor the judgment; extending them to 2029–2031 is expressly an analyst forecast. No minimum count of Increasing or Decreasing labels is imposed.

B39.value: Type describes the nature of the main evidence. Strength describes confidence in relevance and support. Neither a Fact label nor a reputable publisher proves the complete risk scenario. Existing qualitative strength and imported numerical maturity/reliability remain separate judgments; they were not mechanically recalibrated by this update.

B40.value: Export named data tables, not title rows or charts. ER- IDs and S- IDs are stable keys; semicolon plus space separates multi-value IDs. Do not renumber after sorting. Extend Excel tables when adding rows; Dashboard counts update from the main table. Extend Model Scores, Assessment Evidence and link formulas for new risks. New source IDs continue from S-109.

B41.value: Counts describe this research register, not enterprise exposure, probability or financial impact. Chart formulas use the full table regardless of sheet AutoFilter state. The Scope selector filters dashboard aggregation. Qualitative Priority is distinct from the imported numerical External Priority Score.

B42.value: S-12 is withdrawn historical guidance; use current Regulation B S-93 and withdrawal list S-94. S-14 is superseded historical model guidance; S-103/S-108 establish the current banking guidance and its GenAI/agentic exclusion. A banking or global source is not automatically a binding CU requirement.

D6.value: External weights sum to 1. Recalibrate after testing the register.

D7.value: Trigger-to-material-impact interval, not time until risk emerges.

D8.value: Only qualifying distinct downstream mechanisms contribute.

D10.value: Internal and Company indices increase with priority.

D11.value: MAX(m,1−Capability). A technical scoring floor, not measured residual-risk fraction.

D12.value: Positive common normalization threshold. Linear normalization is a prototype; impact scale and threshold still require company agreement.

D13.value: How much of the relevant exposure, activities and failure pathways is covered by the required capability.

D14.value: How quickly required detection, decisions and containment occur within the scenario impact window.

D15.value: How adequate the people, skills, authority, tools and capacity are to execute required actions.

D16.value: How well essential capability continues to work under disruption, stress or loss of a dependency.

D17.value: How effectively required operations and capacity can be restored after disruption.

D18.value: Diagnostic only. Scoring formulas validate their own required settings.

D23.value: Register Priority and Category Rank remain from the base report. External Priority Score is a separate numerical method imported from Priority_Aligned. It does not replace the qualitative ranking.

D24.value: September 18 link/maturity review retained. September 24 update adds dominant evidence types, conditional timing review and 3–5-year outlook. This is a bounded external desk assessment, not an internal control review.

D25.value: Ranks strength of evidence, impact speed and supported propagation. It is neither occurrence probability nor expected monetary loss.

D26.value: Maturity/relevance and source reliability concern the same scenario claim. Do not reward a reliable publisher for evidence that does not validate that claim.

D27.value: Only a hypothesis; the complete working mechanism has not been demonstrated. Unknown evidence is blank, not zero.

D28.value: Working mechanism demonstrated experimentally or in a relevant test.

D29.value: Real-world occurrence/application established; financial-organization applicability not yet established for the complete scenario.

D30.value: Mechanism or material event established in financial operations/organizations.

D31.value: Repeated relevant occurrences established specifically in credit unions. Adoption or theoretical exposure alone is insufficient.

D32.value: For non-adversarial risks, application means occurrence of the defined mechanism. This cross-risk interpretation requires review; do not equate a driver or a policy announcement with realized loss.

D33.value: The claim or evidence is materially falsified or misrepresented; exclude as positive support.

D34.value: Origin known but underlying evidence/verification unclear.

D35.value: Traceable evidence with material limitations in verification or scenario fit.

D36.value: Primary evidence or transparent verification with stated limitations.

D37.value: The 0.75 standard plus independent underlying verification/reproduction. Multiple retellings are not independent evidence.

D38.value: Define claim; locate original evidence; verify origin/date/method; distinguish observed events from forecasts; test sector fit and counter-evidence; assign M and R; multiply; record sources, limitations and date.

D39.value: Use a coherent documented evidence package supporting the same claim. No source-count bonus. Weak ancillary sources do not automatically dilute or strengthen an independently supported claim.

D40.value: Weekly public-source monitoring can revise M or R and the rationale. Availability/freshness and counter-evidence are not additional weighted metrics. No scheduled automation is created by this file.

D41.value: Retained broad band: 0–12 months scores 1.00. Velocity is time from T0 (a specified trigger) to first material adverse impact, excluding time until the trigger. Fine-band evidence is in Velocity Rationale; preserved bands are not all newly validated.

D42.value: Retained broad band: 13–18 months scores 0.67. Require evidence of post-trigger transmission over this interval; implementation or adoption time before T0 does not qualify. Any faster supported pathway is flagged for review.

D43.value: Retained broad band: Over 18 months scores 0.33. Require a supported post-trigger delay. A distant technology or migration deadline alone does not establish slow velocity. Unknown is not scored.

D44.value: Specify T0 and a material adverse endpoint; verify chronology, a binding applicable clock or a defensible operational analogue; distinguish observation from inference; choose the narrowest supported interval. If timing is unsupported, state Insufficient evidence to refine the interval. Do not manufacture a calendar estimate.

D45.value: Risk A must itself act as a driver of distinct B. Each direct link must pass all five checks below. Count distinct B once.

D46.value: Identify the specific change caused by A that triggers or amplifies B. Shared drivers and correlation do not suffice.

D47.value: A source supports that exact mechanism, not merely that both risks exist.

D48.value: No separate risk mediates A → B. Evaluate adjacent steps separately in a cascade.

D49.value: B does not duplicate A or the same event/loss already included in A.

D50.value: Evidence conditions match the defined scenario. Company exposure is assessed separately.

D51.value: Confirmed only if all five pass. A failed criterion means Does not qualify. A material evidence gap means Insufficient evidence; exclude from confirmed count.

D52.value: After the scoped review is complete, zero means no qualifying link established in that scope. Rejected and insufficient-evidence candidates remain visible. It does not prove causal isolation. Incomplete review blocks D and External, rather than substituting zero.

D54.value: One direct B plus a confirmed compatible onward path to distinct C outside A and its direct set.

D55.value: Two distinct confirmed direct downstream risks.

D56.value: Two direct risks plus at least one additional qualifying indirect risk.

D57.value: Cap at 1. Record cascades even when they do not increase the score.

D58.value: Validate all adjacent links and chain compatibility. Exclude duplicates and revisited nodes. Apply uplift once, not per chain, depth or indirect risk.

D59.value: Each candidate has a terminal decision: Confirmed, Excluded, or Insufficient evidence. Not reached means short-circuit after a decisive failed/unestablished criterion. No Pending decisions remain. Research completion is distinct from causal certainty.

D60.value: External = 0.40 × ES + 0.35 × Velocity + 0.25 × Interdependencies. Settings are editable. Missing inputs block the result.

D61.value: Likelihood of a specified event over a consistent horizon and exposure. Scores below are category anchors, not measured probabilities or probability-range boundaries.

D62.value: Judgment must be justified by internal statistics, comparable external data or structured expert evidence.

D63.value: Use the same event definition and horizon across compared risks.

D64.value: Document exposure and the basis of the judgment.

D65.value: State which controls are already reflected in the estimate.

D66.value: Do not interpret the category score as a calibrated annual event frequency.

D67.value: Keep input blank or choose Unknown. Missing evidence must not become zero.

D68.value: Conditional scenario loss in USD divided by a positive company-approved critical loss threshold. Use comparable loss basis and horizon; avoid duplicated downstream losses.

D69.value: Money-to-index shape and threshold remain company decisions. Threshold is blank. No illustrative loss or company impact is prefilled.

D70.value: Confirmed ability to manage a specified scenario: prevent or detect, contain consequences, respond and recover. Higher means better readiness.

D71.value: Assessment establishes required capability is absent. Missing assessment is not zero.

D72.value: Fragmented capability; essential gaps or dependence on individuals.

D73.value: Implemented, but relevant scenario effectiveness insufficiently demonstrated.

D74.value: Relevant testing demonstrates achievement of defined objectives.

D75.value: Effectiveness demonstrated across repeated reviews and relevant changes.

D76.value: Draft C = 0.25 Coverage + 0.20 Timeliness + 0.10 Resources + 0.15 Resilience + 0.10 Recovery + 0.20 Process Adherence. Six component scores use 0–1 and require scenario-specific evidence. These weights are a starting judgment, not calibrated effectiveness.

D77.value: For each risk separately: define scenario, exposure coverage and objectives; collect staffing, execution, test and incident evidence; score all six dimensions; document critical gaps and alternatives. Missing assessment is not zero; do not redistribute missing weights.

D78.value: A weighted mean allows strong dimensions to offset weak ones. Flag critical gaps in narrative. No minimum/cap rule is approved. Do not drop missing components or redistribute weights.

D79.value: C = 1 gives 0.01, never 1. C ≥ 0.99 receives the same minimum modifier. This is a scoring convention, not proven risk reduction.

D80.value: Lower Internal is better, conditional on consistent inputs. A legitimate Impact of zero yields zero. Missing inputs do not.

D81.value: Do not reduce L/I for the same protections and then apply the full capability reduction again. Record a common pre-control basis or justify an explicitly separated control treatment.

D82.value: Company Priority is a blended prioritization index. It is not expected loss. No final company value appears until all internal prerequisites are supplied.

D83.value: Internal Inputs is intentionally omitted and Company Priority columns removed. Likelihood, impact and capability are retained as methodology references only. No current VyStar exposure, capability or company priority is calculated in this workbook.

D84.value: Cross-sheet results use Risk ID. Duplicate/missing IDs block matching outputs. Sort full tables rather than individual columns. Add new risks by extending formulas and lookup ranges.

D85.value: Sources is the master S- ID register. Reviewed Sources retains review limitations under the same IDs; Assessment Evidence links each risk to evidence and timing. Imported maturity/reliability values are preserved, not inferred from Evidence Type.

D86.value: All 34 timing rationales were reviewed September 24. Retained broad bands are unchanged; Unknown fine timing and band conflicts are explicit. A retained numerical score is not new evidence that material harm will occur within its interval.

D87.value: Use a consequential branch in the actual risk definition. Do not substitute transaction execution, task speed or adoption time for first material organizational impact without explaining the causal connection. No internal monetary materiality threshold is assumed.

D88.value: A source-supported channel may qualify under explicitly recorded conditions, without an observed company event. General mechanisms can transfer to AI-origin incidents only when the originating technology does not alter the causal channel. No probability of transmission is implied.

D89.value: All reviewed onward paths fail an edge, distinctness or direct-set condition. Cascade uplift is zero after review, not because the review was skipped. See Cascade Review.

D90.value: Velocity scores vary with the retained base bands. Some bands lack new timing validation; review Assessment Evidence before using score rankings. Evidence availability can under-rank novel risks. No additional confidence multiplier or fine-band score has been silently introduced.

D91.value: M=0: reviewed scenario remains a hypothesis. D=0: no qualifying link in completed scope. Missing metric: blank and result blocked. Source reliability describes the reviewed evidence package, not certainty that a hypothesized event will occur.

D92.value: Read exact scenario; search primary incident/research/supervisory evidence and counter-evidence; classify M/R; specify velocity trigger/endpoint; expand link candidates; apply five gates; check compatible distinct onward paths; compute; validate formulas. Reopen a decision when new relevant evidence changes a gate.

D93.value: Relevant sections and abstracts were retrieved; this is not full re-verification of every historical citation. NBER S-25/S-99 relied on publisher search excerpts where direct access failed. Reviewed Sources identifies inherited-only checks.

D94.value: Weights and normalization are working methodology, not empirically calibrated risk reductions. Reassess cross-risk comparability, materiality, capability dimensions and sensitivity to missing evidence before management decisions.

D96.value: How consistently required procedures and controls are actually followed, supported by execution evidence.

D98.value: Reference scale supplied by the user. Not substituted into Model Scores; broad-band scoring remains unchanged.

D99.value: Reference scale supplied by the user. Not substituted into Model Scores; broad-band scoring remains unchanged.

D100.value: Reference scale supplied by the user. Not substituted into Model Scores; broad-band scoring remains unchanged.

D102.value: Reference scale supplied by the user. Not substituted into Model Scores; broad-band scoring remains unchanged.

D103.value: Reference scale supplied by the user. Not substituted into Model Scores; broad-band scoring remains unchanged.

D104.value: Use either sub-band only when evidence supports the distinction; both remain within reference score 2.

D105.value: Insufficient evidence to refine the interval. Do not derive a number from the technology adoption horizon.

D106.value: A reference score of 6 is not six times the risk. No 6-to-0–1 normalization has been approved or introduced.

A3.value: Canonical S- IDs link to Sources. Imported reviews retain their dates; September 24 checks are explicitly identified. No new R-series IDs.

C6.value: Alert on fraud schemes involving deepfake media

G6.value: BSA and law-enforcement evidence: synthetic identities, stolen PII, subsequent illicit transactions. SAR attribution is qualified; no credit-union-only series.

C7.value: Impact of AI on cyber threat: now to 2027

G7.value: Intelligence/industry assessment of current attacker assistance; forecasts are not observed incidents.

C8.value: Anatomy of a frontier lab agent intrusion

G8.value: Affected party describes a July 9–13 intrusion and platform logs. Nonfinancial case, unusual evaluation configuration; not a general incident frequency.

C9.value: Hugging Face incident and the road ahead

G9.value: Originating party investigation; cross-check S-70. Real external effects during an internal evaluation, not routine customer deployment.

C10.value: Insights on AI agent security from a large-scale red-teaming competition

G10.value: Agent manipulation demonstrated in a test setting; do not classify a test as a financial incident.

C11.value: Money Talks: lessons from two LLM pilots on consumer guidance

G11.value: Controlled studies: some inaccurate outputs and presentation effects; most evaluated definitions were high quality. Context-specific, not production losses.

C12.value: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

G12.value: Recursive-training degradation in experiments. Not a claim that every use of synthetic data degrades a model.

C13.value: Artificial intelligence in UK financial services – 2024

G13.value: 118 responding firms, self-reported adoption and constraints. Provider concentration/opacity are exposures, not proof of losses.

C14.value: Artificial Intelligence: Use and Oversight in Financial Services

G14.value: Document review and interviews identify oversight gaps. Regulatory oversight gaps are not proof of a credit union violating an applicable obligation.

C15.value: Financial Stability in Focus: AI in the financial system

G15.value: Forward-looking analysis of common models, providers, cyber and macro channels. Scenarios are not incident observations.

C16.value: Credit where credit is due: explaining AI credit decisions

G16.value: Experiment shows explanation design can impair error challenge. No finding of an actual lender unlawfully discriminating.

G17.value: Provider discloses cross-user information exposure. Self-reported, nonfinancial-sector event; not evidence of every form of AI leakage.

G18.value: Actual authorship/registration questions; not a finding that every AI output infringes rights or that financial firms incurred loss.

C19.value: Tracking the impact of AI on the labor market

G19.value: No clear relationship between AI exposure/use and recent employment changes established by this analysis. Does not rule out future disruption.

G20.value: Workplace productivity evidence; heterogeneous effects. Does not measure credit-union franchise loss from non-adoption. September 24: publisher search excerpt available; direct page access returned 403.

G21.value: Credit-union supervisory priorities and current pressures; not a quantified causal estimate of cross-rail migration.

C22.value: Review of supervision and regulation of SVB

F22.value: Executive summary; failure and deposit run

G22.value: Realized bank run with rapid withdrawals and networked concentration. Different insurance coverage and depositor structure limit direct CU extrapolation.

G23.value: Borrower-level insurance premium / credit outcome study. Observational identification and geography limit causal transfer.

C24.value: 2025 cybersecurity and credit union system resilience report

G24.value: Credit-union vendor exposure and incidents; does not isolate low substitutability as cause in each case.

F25.value: Commercial real estate and bank funding

G25.value: Current CRE credit/valuation conditions; improving measures are counter-evidence to a universal deterioration claim.

G26.value: Conditional deposit replacement/funding volatility channel. Significant retail deposit outflows were not yet observed in the discussion. Imported review dated 2026-09-18; not independently re-opened in the September 24 update.

C27.value: Personal Financial Data Rights compliance resources

G27.value: Dates stayed October 29, 2025; reconsideration underway. Do not treat original 1033 deadlines as presently binding.

G28.value: Tracks legislation, including bills; proposed bills must not be counted as enacted duties.

G29.value: GLBA financial-institution/data exemption illustrates why applicability must be checked. Not a nationwide exemption conclusion.

F30.value: Staffing, backlog and digital-payment monitoring findings

G30.value: Enforcement record links resourcing deficiencies to monitoring gaps; P2P monitoring deficiencies separately documented. One bank, not a sector prevalence estimate.

C31.value: A two-sided affair: banks and tech firms in banking

G31.value: Platform relationships, simultaneous withdrawals and less-sticky platform deposits. International examples require comparable arrangements.

G32.value: Planning guidance, not date of quantum arrival or measured trigger-to-loss velocity.

C33.value: Quantum-readiness for the financial system: a roadmap

G33.value: Layered technical dependencies and migration planning. Need does not demonstrate realized migration failure. Imported review dated 2026-09-18; not independently re-opened in the September 24 update.

G34.value: Observed access differences; survey may undercount digitally excluded respondents. Age is not proof of scam susceptibility.

C35.value: Operational resilience in a macroprudential framework

G35.value: Service/data incidents can impair confidence and trigger runs. Communication/workarounds may contain effects; causal channels are conditional.

C36.value: Rising property insurance costs and pass-through to rents

G36.value: Apartment insurance increases associated with lower owner income. Refinancing failure is not directly demonstrated by this study. Imported review dated 2026-09-18; not independently re-opened in the September 24 update.

C37.value: 2023 banking turmoil and the Bank Term Funding Program

G37.value: Funding substitution following withdrawals. Does not establish every historical deposit model became structurally invalid.

G38.value: Technical risk taxonomy and mitigations. Individual experiments/incidents are preferred for maturity scoring.

C39.value: Stablecoins: growth potential and impact on banking

G39.value: Funding effects depend on reserve design. Corrects the unrelated URL stored as original S-45.

C40.value: Sound practices for responsible AI adoption: consultation

G40.value: Consultation and prospective vulnerabilities, not binding rules or measured agent-driven disintermediation.

G41.value: Current notification requirements; not a measured litigation or loss duration.

G42.value: Confirms withdrawal of Circular 2023-03; does not repeal Regulation B.

C43.value: Commissioner approves significant rate decreases for homeowners

G43.value: Florida counter-evidence to extrapolating nationwide historical premium increases; selected policies, not every borrower.

C44.value: New property and casualty insurers: 20 entrants since reforms

G44.value: New authorized insurers support a capacity-recovery signal; not proof that catastrophe or affordability risk is resolved.

G45.value: Instant settlement mechanism; not a measured fraud prevalence or guaranteed inability to recover funds.

G46.value: Observed financial-service outage analogue; not AI-specific and not a credit-union incident.

G47.value: Publisher search excerpt supports productivity improvement during early months. Direct page access returned 403; no measured CU competitive-loss interval.

G48.value: Current migration guidance. Readiness lead time does not establish time from quantum compromise to material harm.

C49.value: Regulation and supervision of the financial sector in the age of artificial intelligence

G49.value: Prospective agentic-finance channel; not evidence of realized member disintermediation.

Priority is the retained qualitative classification; the numerical model is on Model Scores.</t></si><si><t>WHAT NEEDS CAREFUL INTERPRETATION</t></si><si><t>20 finer timing estimates remain unvalidated; ER-7 needs a broad-band review. These are whole-register findings. See Assessment Evidence.</t></si><si><t>Original priorities and broad velocity bands are retained. Source withdrawals, scope exclusions and geographic counter-evidence are recorded in the relevant rationale fields.</t></si><si><t>CHART DATA • FORMULA-DRIVEN</t></si><si><t>Risk Category</t></si><si><t>Count</t></si><si><t>Priority</t></si><si><t>Evidence Strength</t></si><si><t>Risk Velocity</t></si><si><t>Operational</t></si><si><t>Immediate</t></si><si><t>High</t></si><si><t>0–12 months</t></si><si><t>Compliance / Legal</t></si><si><t>Near-Term</t></si><si><t>Medium</t></si><si><t>13–18 months</t></si><si><t>Strategic</t></si><si><t>Monitor</t></si><si><t>Low</t></si><si><t>Over 18 months</t></si><si><t>Credit</t></si><si><t>Watch / Validate</t></si><si><t>Unknown</t></si><si><t>Interest Rate</t></si><si><t>Liquidity</t></si><si><t>Reputation</t></si><si><t>Risk Outlook</t></si><si><t>Research Scope</t></si><si><t>Increasing</t></si><si><t>AI-related</t></si><si><t>Constant</t></si><si><t>Non-AI</t></si><si><t>Decreasing</t></si><si><t>Emerging risks for U.S. credit unions</t></si><si><t>VyStar ERM | External research | Updated September 24, 2026 | Outlook: 2029–2031</t></si><si><t>Purpose and scope</t></si><si><t>A source-backed external register for ERM analysts to assess, map, link or reject during a later VyStar-specific phase. The workbook does not assess current exposure, controls, owners, residual risk or actual register matches. The seven supplied risk categories are preserved.</t></si><si><t>Method and use</t></si><si><t>34 scenarios across the seven supplied categories. Evidence Type has one dominant value; supporting nuance remains in Assessment Evidence. Broad velocity, qualitative priority and IDs are preserved. Outlook is a forecast of external pressure. Numerical model scores are a separate methodology reference, not VyStar risk exposure.</t></si><si><t>Theme</t></si><si><t>What the evidence indicates</t></si><si><t>ERM implication</t></si><si><t>Related Risk ID(s)</t></si><si><t>Source ID(s)</t></si><si><t>Cross-cutting</t></si><si><t>Fraud and payment controls face simultaneous pressure from synthetic impersonation and faster movement across payment rails.</t></si><si><t>Coordinate identity, authentication, payment and recovery monitoring rather than treating each scheme or rail as isolated.</t></si><si><t>ER-1; ER-20</t></si><si><t>S-9; S-10; S-11; S-36; S-39; S-53; S-54; S-65</t></si><si><t>Critical-provider concentration is a shared operational vulnerability; AI adds hidden model, cloud and data dependencies to existing core, telecom and payment concentration.</t></si><si><t>Map services through fourth parties, test substitutability and require material-change disclosure.</t></si><si><t>ER-6; ER-7; ER-23</t></si><si><t>S-2; S-3; S-17; S-52; S-62; S-64</t></si><si><t>Digital channels compress deposit-outflow velocity even when aggregate system liquidity appears stable.</t></si><si><t>Use intraday scenarios, pre-positioned collateral and same-day escalation authority.</t></si><si><t>ER-21</t></si><si><t>S-39; S-40; S-55; S-56</t></si><si><t>Agentic execution, model unreliability and unexplained decisioning can turn an information error into an operational, legal or member-impacting action.</t></si><si><t>Separate agents from chatbots in inventories; constrain authority; validate consequential outputs and adverse-action reasons.</t></si><si><t>ER-3; ER-4; ER-9</t></si><si><t>S-2; S-72; S-73; S-93; S-94; S-103; S-108</t></si><si><t>Historical insurance cost stress can affect borrower cash flow and collateral. Current Florida rate reductions and insurer entry create important geographic counter-evidence; the net outlook is Unknown.</t></si><si><t>Segment collateral by insurance conditions and test escrow/payment shocks and coverage lapse.</t></si><si><t>ER-22</t></si><si><t>S-42; S-43; S-95; S-96</t></si><si><t>CRE refinancing pressure and changed deposit behavior remain uneven but actionable balance-sheet risks.</t></si><si><t>Re-underwrite near maturities and back-test deposit beta, decay and migration assumptions against the latest cycle.</t></si><si><t>ER-24; ER-25</t></si><si><t>S-39; S-40; S-41; S-56; S-68</t></si><si><t>Governance and data duties continue to evolve, but developments do not all increase obligations. CFPB withdrew Circular 2023-03; revised bank model guidance excludes GenAI and agentic AI.</t></si><si><t>Maintain a formal horizon scan and reusable governance, consent, data and evidence controls; sequence rule-specific investment by confirmed status.</t></si><si><t>ER-8; ER-10; ER-26; ER-27; ER-28; ER-29</t></si><si><t>S-3; S-81; S-92; S-93; S-94; S-103; S-108</t></si><si><t>Competition for the member interface is shifting through AI service, embedded finance, open banking and tokenized payments.</t></si><si><t>Track relationship, deposit and channel effects while preserving human access and trusted advice.</t></si><si><t>ER-17; ER-19; ER-26; ER-30</t></si><si><t>S-17; S-19; S-44; S-45; S-66</t></si><si><t>Workforce capability is both an opportunity and a control-capacity constraint; AI may improve productivity while increasing the need for governance and specialist skills.</t></si><si><t>Build role-specific capability and monitor key-person, vacancy, override and quality indicators without assuming broad displacement.</t></si><si><t>ER-18; ER-32</t></si><si><t>S-24; S-25; S-26; S-58; S-59</t></si><si><t>Long lead</t></si><si><t>PQC migration, demographic change and AI labor/macro channels warrant monitoring. Their adoption horizons do not establish the event-to-material-impact interval.</t></si><si><t>Use milestone-based monitoring and scenario analysis; do not convert uncertain timelines into false precision.</t></si><si><t>ER-12; ER-14; ER-31; ER-33</t></si><si><t>S-18; S-20; S-24; S-50; S-51; S-60; S-61</t></si><si><t>Major uncertainties</t></si><si><t>Credit-union-specific incident and adoption evidence remains limited. Fine timing is unvalidated for 20 scenarios; ER-7 has a faster outage pathway than its retained broad band. Outlook is Unknown for 11 risks, including AI labor-to-credit transmission, Florida insurance and several balance-sheet or regulatory pathways. Unknown is not evidence of stability.
